blockers.claim: The fail-closed rule requires both named consent and a recorded host-effect contract instance before an in-scope host act can escape UNEXERCISABLE.
blockers.evidence: failClosed.rule denies only an act with 'no named consent AND no recorded contract instance.' In Boolean terms, denial is (!consent && !instance), so either consent alone or an instance alone makes the denial predicate false. Adopted D-032 instead makes the host-effect contract necessary, not sufficient, in addition to action consent and product admission. The subject never defines 'recorded contract instance,' and its authorityClaim describes this JSON as the contract, creating a second ambiguity between the design contract and a per-invocation authorization record.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define the design contract separately from a per-invocation authorization record. State the gate positively and conjunctively: an act is exercisable only when this contract is adopted/recorded by the joint owners, a valid action-scoped consent or policy authorization record exists, every product/slice prerequisite is satisfied, and the subtype is classified. Equivalently, absence of ANY required condition denies. Add fixtures for consent-without-contract, contract-without-consent, and consent-plus-contract-without-product-admission.

blockers.claim: This is the scoped host-effect authorization contract D-032 requires.
blockers.evidence: The consent object lists two carrier names and one lifecycle sentence but defines no authorization-record shape, decision vocabulary, or per-class scope. It does not bind invocation id, check ids, exact external-tool identity, exact probe resources, endpoint set, platform, policy provenance, or owner/product-admission references. It also says cancel or process death 'ends' consent without an effect-commit boundary, ordering rule, cleanup rule, or audit obligation. Doctor v4 already makes those scope distinctions load-bearing. A list of covered acts plus three outcome labels is not an executable authorization contract and cannot decide whether a particular attempted effect was authorized.
blockers.requiredRepair: Add a closed per-invocation authorization-record schema carrying actor, action class/subtype, exact invocation/check/resource/tool/endpoint/platform scope, consent carrier and policy provenance, product-admission references, granted/denied resolution, owner, and audit identity. Define reversible and irreversible/effect-commit boundaries, cancellation/process-death ordering, cleanup, and the rule that no not-yet-committed effect may commit after authorization ends. Supply executable fixtures for scope mismatch, wildcard refusal, cancellation on each side of commit, and process death with unknown outcome.

blockers.claim: The three host outcomes compose with the accepted doctor-v4 post-report contract and therefore carry BLK-3 honestly.
blockers.evidence: Doctor v4 requires one consent record per attempted consented action and separates authorization, confinement execution, result, residualLimitation, effectOutcome, and enforcementDisclosure. effectOutcome is the reserved binding point the actor decision must resolve; enforcementDisclosure must be withdrawn if host actors remain outside DR-105; permissionRef remains reserved. The subject mentions none of these members and does not state where COMPLETED, DEFINITELY_NOT_PERFORMED, or INDETERMINATE is serialized. FC-OUTCOME merely says the labels are distinguishable 'in the post-report' without a field, schema, mapping, or oracle. Thus an implementation can satisfy this artifact in prose while leaving doctor v4's required effectOutcome reserved/unpopulated, or can incorrectly put the value in execution/result. That is the narration defect BLK-3 exists to prevent.
blockers.requiredRepair: Normatively bind the host vocabulary to doctor-v4 consentRecords[].effectOutcome; preserve authorization/execution/result/residualLimitation as separate axes; keep permissionRef permanently reserved for host acts; and explicitly withdraw or define the host treatment of enforcementDisclosure under D-032 Option B. Require an effectOutcome value for every attempted host effect when knowable and an explicit INDETERMINATE value, never a refusal or prose-only residual, when not. Turn FC-OUTCOME into field-level fixtures that reject wrong-axis and prose-only encodings.

blockers.claim: CA-4 remains fail-closed while the slice-1 doctor egress execution side is unsettled.
blockers.evidence: coveredActs.CA-4-host says the host-versus-component execution side is UNSETTLED, then permits host CA-4 'unless explicitly consented and this contract instance exists.' Before actor classification, the same egress may actually be component-originated and therefore require DR-105/PT-NET-EGRESS. Host consent cannot lawfully substitute for that component permission. D-032 leaves the execution-side choice to this contract; this candidate does not make the choice yet lets the effect proceed.
blockers.requiredRepair: Either classify each slice-1 doctor egress path at exact implementation/actor boundaries, with component-originated paths remaining exclusively in DR-105, or keep every unsettled path unexercisable regardless of host consent. Remove the 'unless' bypass. Add a fixture proving an unclassified egress cannot run and actor relabeling cannot change the required authorization after the request is accepted.

blockers.claim: The contract preserves D-032's rule that it is necessary but not sufficient for product admission across every covered host act.
blockers.evidence: CA-1 names DR-G21/manifest, CA-2 names DR-119 and DR-117/128, and KEYCHAIN names DR-108. OUT_OF_ROOT_READ, LOCAL_SOCKET_OR_PIPE, and PRIVILEGED_PLATFORM_FACILITY each route only to 'this contract.' No separate D-002/product/slice selector, owner decision, or explicit UNOWNED state exists for them. Combined with the failClosed.rule Boolean, consent plus this contract can be read as sufficient to exercise all three surfaces, silently turning an authorization-mechanics artifact into product admission authority.
blockers.requiredRepair: For every CA-3 subtype, name the separate product/slice authority and exact admission evidence, or mark the authority UNOWNED with a required D-000 owner-assignment decision. State that this contract cannot admit a surface and that the subtype remains unexercisable until both admission and authorization layers resolve. Add negative fixtures for a valid consent/contract with absent product admission.
